intuition: Track the farthest position you can reach. When you visit a reachable position, its jump length may extend that distance. You do not need to remember the route. If you reach a position beyond the farthest reachable point, no earlier jump can cross that gap.

All currently reachable indices form a continuous prefix beginning at zero. Keep only its farthest endpoint. Scanning a reachable index extends that endpoint to the larger of the old frontier and i+nums[i]. There is no benefit in retaining the routes that created the frontier.

If the next index lies beyond farthest, no earlier processed jump can cross that gap; later positions cannot help because they are unreachable too. Conversely, once farthest reaches the last index, some sequence of legal jumps already reaches the goal, and the scan can end immediately.

steps: For nums=[2,3,1,1,4], initialize farthest=0: the starting position is reachable without jumping.
At i=0, jump=2 extends the frontier to 2. Indices 1 and 2 are now reachable landing positions.
At i=1, first verify 1<=2. This position is inside the reachable prefix, so its jump can be considered.
Its maximum landing index is 1+3=4. Updating farthest gives 4, expanding the known prefix through the goal.
The final index is 4, so return true now. A concrete successful route is 0→1→4.

codeNotes.note: This comparison detects an unreachable gap before reading that position as a possible launch point; using its jump would invent a route.
A weaker current jump must never shrink earlier reachability. The maximum retains every landing position already established by previous indices.
Jump lengths are upper bounds, so crossing the final index also permits landing on it using a shorter jump.

keyDecision: Visit index i only if i <= farthest. Update farthest with i + nums[i].
